overview: White fianchettoes the king's bishop to pressure the long diagonal, and Black mirrors with ...Bb7 and contests e4. The main line goes 4...Bb7 5.Bg2 Be7 6.O-O O-O 7.Nc3 Ne4, where Black trades a pair of knights to ease the cramp. Play is a long manoeuvring fight over e4, with small edges and few early tactics.

white_ideas.idea: Bg2, O-O, Nc3 and Qc2 or d5 to gain space, using the bishop on the long diagonal.
Break with e4 or d5 to seize the centre.

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto on b7 and control e4 with ...Ne4 and ...Bb7 to fight the diagonal.
Strike with ...c5 or ...d5 at the right moment.

typical_structures.structure: Fianchettoed bishops on g2 and b7, centre pawns on d4/c4 against d6/e6, tension over e4.

character.notes: Mainly strategic, with trades and few forcing lines. It is hard to break down.

soundness.notes: Very sound; a main line of the Queen's Indian.

structure.notes: Centre fluid; neither side commits d5 or e4 early.

approach.notes: A mainstream line played by top players.

level.notes: Little to memorise, but the subtle fight for e4 needs positional judgement.

sublines_that_differ.name: Nimzowitsch Variation
sublines_that_differ.how: Black goes for the c4 pawn with a sharper, more tactical game.

character.reason: A sound, hard-to-break set-up with trades and few forcing lines.

soundness.reason: Main line of a respected defence.

structure.reason: The centre is undecided, as in the QID and Catalan.

approach.reason: A mainstream response, not a set-up against everything.

level.reason: Plans over theory, with mid-level subtlety.
